episodes.214634: An upper high over Arizona and Utah on August 2nd pivoted back east towards New Mexico on August 3rd. Intense daytime heating due to record temperatures for early August combined with marginal moisture resulted in the development of high based showers and storms across the northeast and central highlands during the afternoon and early evening hours. One of these high based showers resulted in a 62 mph dry microburst wind gust over the ASOS at Clines Corners.
episodes.214686: A frontal boundary advanced through northeastern NM and washed up to the east slopes of the central mountain chain during the morning of August 4th. Daily rounds of afternoon thunderstorms were able to develop along the mountain chain August 4th through 6th, with several producing large or accumulating hail over portions of northeastern and central NM. One storm produced large hail over Philmont Scout Ranch on the 4th, with another producing severe hail near Folsom on the 5th, and a third producing accumulating hail and minor flooding impacts along NM3 just north of Encino, NM on the 6th. Additionally, a landspout was observed by a driver on Interstate 25 near Wagon Mound along the leading edge of an approaching severe warned thunderstorm on August 5th. Shower and thunderstorm activity dissipated during the evening hours each day.
episodes.216180: A stalled front was the focal point for scattered showers and thunderstorms during the evening and overnight hours of August third to the early morning hours of August fourth. Shower and thunderstorm activity moved from southwest to northeast across the Pamlico Sound and coastal waters during this timeframe. With ample instability in place a few of these storms became strong to severe in nature bringing strong wind gusts to portions of the Pamlico Sound.
episodes.216294: Heavy training thunderstorms brought flooding to the Pea Island area of Hatteras Island. Four to six inches of rain fell in a short period of time here. This prompted the closure of Hwy 12 for a time.
episodes.217362: Severe thunderstorms produced hail up to the size of ping pong balls during the morning. Additional severe thunderstorms developed in the evening over parts of Clearwater County and Beltrami Counties producing large hail to the size of quarters and damaging winds.
episodes.217375: A closed upper level low was located across interior portions of the Southeast on August 4. This helped create widespread showers and storms in the vicinity of a stationary front draped across portions of south-central and southeastern Virginia. Given a tropical airmass in place with very high precipitable water values of 2-2.4 inches and high humidity, showers and storms were slow-movers and created very heavy rainfall rates. This resulted in heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.217426: A surface boundary spawned a small cluster of thunderstorms moving eastward across Southwest Nebraska during the early and mid-evening hours. A 73 mph wind gust was measured 12 miles NW of Max, Nebraska.
episodes.217600: On the evening of August 3rd, 2026, a round of severe thunderstorms swept across northern Minnesota, bringing damaging straight-line winds to Koochiching and St. Louis counties. Koochiching County recorded wind gusts exceeding 65 mph near Margie, knocking down trees and disrupting local infrastructure. As the storm complex pushed eastward into St. Louis County, strong gusts triggered multiple reports of downed trees around Lake Vermilion and Tower.
episodes.217706: A stalled frontal boundary to the northwest of the region, combined with the usual late summer daytime heating/influences of sea breezes, resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms across the area. Precipitable Water (PWAT) values reached as high as 2.2 to 2.5 inches during this period, which strongly supported heavy rain and flooding potential.
episodes.218376: A period of persistent, heavy rainfall impacted the Susitna Valley in early August 2026, leading to excessive runoff and rapidly rising rivers. This resulted in moderate flooding across both the Western and Central Susitna Valley. The most severe impacts were concentrated along the Yentna River basin, where Lake Creek surged to its second-highest crest on record, forcing emergency evacuations of local wilderness lodges. Simultaneously, heavy rainfall overwhelmed local creeks and drainage infrastructure in the Petersville area, resulting in inundated roadways and washed-out culverts, while rapid rises on Moose Creek sent overland flow spilling across Oilwell Road. Further downstream, increased flows exacerbated riverbank erosion along the Skwentna River.
episodes.218418: An active monsoon day brought severe thunderstorms across portions of Southeastern Arizona that caused numerous trees to be damaged or uprooted, recorded wind gusts ranging from 58 to 88 mph, damage to roofs and homes, downed power lines that caused power outages, and 1 inch diameter hail. Additionally, there was flash flooding due to locally heavy rainfall from thunderstorms that caused roadways to become impassable.
episodes.218588: An outflow boundary originating from strong thunderstorms north of Cuba propagated northward, focusing new thunderstorm development moving north through the Lower Florida Keys.  Scattered gale-force wind gusts and several waterspouts were observed.
episodes.218589: Convective cloud lines developed along the Gulf of America and Florida Bay sides of the Lower and Upper Florida Keys.  Isolated waterspouts were observed.

Heavy rainfall totaling between 2 and 3 inches overwhelmed local creeks and drainages in the Petersville area. Cache Creek rose approximately 5 feet, resulting in significant overbank flooding that overtopped local roadways and washed out a culvert near the New Cache Creek Cabins. Adjacent Nugget Creek also experienced significant rises and general flooding. By the late afternoon of August 4, observers reported water moving across Petersville Road in at least four separate locations, and social media videos documented extremely high, dangerous flows on Peters Creek. The rising waters and inundated low-water crossings prompted locals to preemptively evacuate the Petersville area.
